transcript.text:
Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for being here. As you all know, our eighth-grade civics class has proposed an oral-history project where all 20 students, J1 through J20, would interview 20 community members, I1 through I20, about local history. The draft plan calls for students to audio record the interviews on their personal phones, publish all 20 recordings on the public school website, and retain the files indefinitely.

Before any interviews can begin, I need to approve this project. District policy requires that our approval packet include current findings from three of you regarding student eligibility, consent, recording technology, storage, and retention: the project advisor, the school counselor, and the instructional technology coordinator. The packet is due to the district office before the first interview date and must be signed by all three of you.

So I'd like to go around and hear from each of you. Could you share your current findings and any concerns about this project? Let's start with the project advisor, then the school counselor, and finally the instructional technology coordinator.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to share an important finding from my roster review. Only eight students have completed the district's media-ethics training: J1, J3, J6, J8, J11, J14, J17, and J20. Only those eight may conduct recorded interviews, and the approval file must include a training-verification record. This means the draft plan's proposal to have all 20 students conduct interviews cannot proceed as written.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I'd like to share my findings from the family-consent review. My review confirms that five interviewees — I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18 — have not granted permission for public web publication. Their recordings may be used only in the school's internal archive. The other 15 interviewees may be included in public publication. The approval plan must include a consent-exclusion record documenting these exclusions. This means the draft plan's proposal to publish all 20 recordings on the public school website cannot proceed as written — only 15 may be publicly published, and the remaining 5 must be restricted to internal archival use.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, my technology review raises several concerns with the draft plan. First, personal phones cannot be used for school recordings. The project must use district tablets instead. Second, all source files must be stored in the restricted OralHistory drive, not on personal devices or general school servers. Third, recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation — indefinite retention is not permitted. Finally, the technology plan must include a secure-storage configuration record documenting these arrangements. This means the draft plan's proposals regarding personal phones, public website storage, and indefinite retention cannot proceed as written.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: Include training-verification record in the approval packet confirming that only J1, J3, J6, J8, J11, J14, J17, and J20 have completed media-ethics training.
Include consent-exclusion record in the approval packet documenting that I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18 are restricted to internal archival use only.
Include secure-storage configuration record in the approval packet documenting use of district tablets, restricted OralHistory drive storage, and 45-day deletion schedule.
Submit the completed approval packet with all three required signatures before the first interview date.
